featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Pawar-Master Reviewer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sometimes it becomes really tough to distinguish between stale fishes and a fresh catch. It can grow harder especially for newbies and upcoming kitchen enthusiasts just like me. But recently I have found my saviour to this problem! And that's 'Cambay Tiger'. No, it is not associated with Onitsuka Tiger in any way :)
Cambay Tiger is a premium store that offers wide range of fresh fishes and different types of meat to choose from.
I got to know from the manager that their  parent company is into this business since 1997. That makes them almost a 30 years old entity in this space.
Initially they became famous for their fresh & enormous sized Tiger Prawns and thus 'Tiger' in their store name.
I have been buying all my meat and seafood essentials from this store only since past 3-4 months and I just adore the service and quality I get every time.
They have their own aquaculture farm so you can be rest assured about the quality of the meat, its freshness and back tracking any product if you wish to.
They follow a 'farm-to-fork' business model and so you can get all your cooking needs under one roof, be it meat, fishes, spices, ready to cook curries, masalas etc.
All the fishes and meat products are cleaned thoroughly before packing them in the most hygienic fashion.
All in all, it's THE BEST place to go if you are looking for a one-stop-shop for your fish and meat requirements.
100% approved and recommended!

Cheers!!

featured_reviews.name: Vedant Raut (Vedanta)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

- Chicken Sukka thali - 5 stars 🤩- Delicious gravy with softest chicken.

- Egg Biryani  - 5 stars🤩  - Long grained rice with perfect blend of spices and 2 boiled eggs.

featured_reviews.name: Shadab Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
(Officially Rajiv Gandhi Sea Link — World-Class Infrastructure Review: Hindi + English Mix)

Bandra-Worli Sea Link is one of India’s most iconic modern bridges — a symbol of engineering excellence and a functional marvel that changed how people travel across Mumbai’s western coastline. It connects Bandra (Western Suburbs) to Worli (South Mumbai) over the Arabian Sea and was designed to reduce traffic congestion and travel time dramatically.  ￼

📏 Technical & Structural Highlights:
• Length: Approximately 5.6 km, making it one of India’s longest sea bridges.  ￼
• Lanes: 8 lanes (4 in each direction) for cars and light vehicles.  ￼
• Design: Cable-stayed main spans with concrete-steel precast segments on either side — an advanced hybrid design.  ￼
• Height: The cable-stay towers rise about 126 m (like a 40+ storey building).  ￼
• Built by Hindustan Construction Company under MSRDC direction after ~9 years of construction (2000–2009).  ￼

🕰 History & Purpose:
Planning for the sea link started decades ago to ease congestion along the old Mahim Causeway route. Over 23 traffic signals were typical between Bandra and Worli before — now the Sea Link cuts that journey from sometimes 40–60 minutes down to ~10 minutes at peak hours.  ￼

🚗 Traffic & Usage:
• The bridge handles tens of thousands of vehicles daily (recent traffic has grown ~33 % year-over-year as of 2025).  ￼
• Only cars and light vehicles are allowed — two-wheelers (bikes) are not permitted due to safety and speed considerations.  ￼
• The maximum speed limit is typically around 80 km/h, and driving beyond can be dangerous (and illegal) — incidents of supercars being reprimanded for speeding have been reported.  ￼

💰 Toll & Fees:
There’s a toll to use the bridge, and rates have increased over time (around ₹85–₹145 depending on vehicle type per one-way trip, with hikes implemented in recent years).  ￼

📍 Visitor & Local Experience:
• The Sea Link is open 24/7, and people love night drives when the city lights reflect off the water, offering breathtaking views.  ￼
• Locals often enjoy the drive for photography, sunset views, and skyline scenes.  ￼
• It’s considered one of Mumbai’s must-experience drives for both residents and visitors.  ￼

⚠️ Notes & Tips:
• No stopping or parking on the bridge — it’s meant for fast uninterrupted travel.  ￼
• Heavy traffic growth means sometimes slight delays during rush hours.  ￼

📌 Overall Verdict:
Bandra-Worli Sea Link is not just a transport route — it’s a cultural and architectural landmark of Mumbai. It blends world-class engineering, practical utility, and a beautiful scenic experience into one drive. Whether you’re a commuter or a tourist, crossing this bridge — especially at sunset or night — is truly a memorable Mumbai experience.  ￼

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

JSW Centre, located in the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) of Mumbai, serves as the corporate headquarters for JSW Group, one of India's leading conglomerates with interests spanning steel, energy, infrastructure, cement, and more.

Architectural Highlights
The JSW Centre is recognized as one of Mumbai's largest open office complexes. Its architectural design features two elliptical structures that merge seamlessly, reflecting a blend of modern aesthetics and functionality. The building incorporates advanced sustainable technologies and contemporary office configurations.

From below the building looks like a ship. There is a well maintained cafeteria/canteen at the first floor (also called atrium floor). I had Espresso coffee there and I can confidently say it was great. The aroma, the taste, everything was awesome. The food at the Canteen is also delicious. There is a central hollow space around which the offices are built.

Overall the office complex is very well maintained, well furnished, neat and clean. The toilets are of International standard and very clean.

Strategic Location
Situated in the heart of Mumbai's financial district, the Bandra Kurla Complex, JSW Centre benefits from excellent connectivity and proximity to major business hubs.

The only con I noticed was that there was no place for visitors to sit in front of the building or even at the reception at the ground floor. So unless you are at the reception in the Atrium floor there is no where you can sit. This is really inconvenient and inconsiderate.

featured_reviews.name: Ankita Mukul Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
Got to know about this place via Google as I was in BKC and wanted to eat fish, looking at the rating I thought of visiting this place.
The place is quite small and gives homely feeling, looking at this i got happy thinking the food would be really nice and homemade.
We ordered for a chicken thali, a pomfret thali and an surmai thali and a tisrya sukkah.
Was totally disappointed when the food came, the tisrya sukkha seemed like tisrya masala and was very sweet. The surmai thali was not upto the mark, surmai was very small, I have never had such small piece of surmai in any of the fish outlet.
Quantity wise I was totally disappointed, chicken thali had just 2 pieces of chicken.
Sol kadhi seemed to be like water added to it, we had reached around 2:30-2:45pm and I think we were served the left over food as it was closing time.
I will not recommend this restaurant to anyone, specially who is a fish lover.

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Amrute
featured_reviews.review_text:
In Mumbai, people are often misguided into thinking Mangalorean or Goan Cuisine as Malvani.. But not here…!!

So I came here today with a friend. He ordered a Tisrya (Clams) Thali and I called for Mori (Shark) Thali. Both were excellent. The fish was fresh and the gravy was very tasty and perfectly spiced. The quantity in each thali was perfect for one adult. If at all I have to complain then I would say, I missed the small portion of Suka Jawla (dry baby shrimp) that is also served as part of the seafood thali in my town.

The service was prompt and the staff was welcoming. Hygiene is taken care of. The place is tiny and very modestly done up, so if you value the ambience as much as your food, then this isn't the place for you. Free Street Parking is available.

If you are craving for good authentic Malvani Food… Sadichha is just the place for you.

featured_reviews.review_text: What a find this place. It's located just opp the MIG club...it's a quaint tiny lil place..serving seafood like a boss! We ordered everything and lived everything. The bombil fry, prawns, mandeli, the pomfret stuffed with prawns (awesomeness) and all the thalis..we had prawn, mory, clams, surmai and pomfret thalis..and for vegetarians with us they specially made some pithala and a good veg thali :).
